note: Corps of Engineers park on Bull Shoals Lake at the US 160 bridge in Theodosia: two small, open loops on a low point either side of a boat-ramp lot, beside a private marina and resort. Little shade; the lake is in plain view from most pads across the loop road and a bare, sloping bank that widens as the pool drops. Swim area and playground. --Claude
summary: rec.gov read (USACE's own pages refused, unread): season May 1-Sept 29, $24 a single site (the stored $16 low is a non-electric rate key no site uses; $26 not found), 20 site records 30-46 ft all with 30 A and water, flush toilets. WATERFRONT (stored lakeview; no change): counted on the 0.24 m/px frame with site coordinates plotted, imagery at a drawn-down pool. Loop B is open ground with a handful of trees. B09 and B08 are nearest the water: about 55 m from the waterline in the image, with the loop road and then a bare bank between, and the paved boat-ramp lot directly beside B08 (day use between pad and water). B15/B16 is about 60 m back behind a gravel work yard and the marina lot. Loop A's A10, A13 and A14 look down a bare slope to the water about 100 m off in this image. Bull Shoals is a flood-control pool that swings many feet, so the gap changes, but at every pad the loop road lies between pad and bank. On an open apron within 50 m with nothing between: none. Clear open views from most pads: lakeview is right.
